newsitem.title: USA: Springs Q2 EPS includes $0.07/shr charge.
newsitem.headline: Springs Q2 EPS includes $0.07/shr charge.

text.p: Springs Industries Inc's said Tuesday its second-quarter earnings of $15.1 million, or $0.73 a share included a $0.07 a share restructuring charge.
Chief executive Walter Elisha said in a statement the charge "obscured improvement over last year's results."
Without the $2.2 million charge, the company earned $0.80 a share, compared with $0.78 last year before extraordinary gains and charges.

Springs posted net income of $39.4 million, or $1.93 a share, in the second quarter of 1996, including a $50.1 million gain or $2.45 a share from selling its Clark-Schwebel division and a restructuring charge and other write-offs totaling $26.6 million or $1.30 a share.

The company's $0.80 earnings per share excluding the charge did not meet analysts' expectations. An April 15 First Call consensus estimate of 9 brokers put the company's second-quarter earnings at $0.84 a share.
Springs reported $528.9 million in revenues in the second quarter, compared with $540.2 million the year before.

Springs said its home furnishings segment, which accounts for 85 percent of its sales, reported a two-percent increase in revenues. Operating earnings before the restructuring charge rose more than 25 percent over last year's second-quarter.

The company said sales of specialty fabrics were down 12 percent from a year ago and "operating earnings declined precipitously." It attributed the results to weak demand and recent customer bankruptcy filings.
Springs' stock traded at 51-1/2 Tuesday afternoon, up 3/4.
